body:
## Summary

- Adds a \`needs_simulation_context\` trait that returns \`true\` for \`ContinuousBoundaryFunction\` and \`DiscreteBoundaryFunction\` BC conditions (fills that require \`clock\`/\`model_fields\`) and \`false\` for everything else, including \`Open\` OBC types
- Guards \`fill_halo_regions!(v)\` in \`set_to_field!\` so it is skipped when the source field carries a CBF/DBF BC — previously this crashed when \`fill_halo_regions!\` was called without clock on such a field
- Guards \`fill_halo_regions!(to_field)\` in \`interpolate!\` similarly, using \`fill_open_bcs=false\` so the distributed MPI exchange still runs for OBC fields while clock-dependent fills are skipped
- Short-circuits \`on_architecture\` in \`set_to_field!\` when architectures already match, avoiding spurious \`ImmersedBoundaryGrid\` reconstruction that triggered \`materialize_immersed_boundary\` → unguarded \`fill_halo_regions!\` on uninitialized MultiRegion connectivity
- Exports \`needs_simulation_context\` from \`BoundaryConditions\`

New test file \`test/test_set_field_interpolation.jl\` covers interpolation correctness, the copy path, all \`needs_simulation_context\` dispatch cases (CBF Flux, Open+DBF, Open+number, FieldBCs), and the CBF-destination crash. All 11 tests pass on CPU.

## Update 1

\`fill_normal_flow_bcs=false\` was blanket-skipping the fill for all NormalFlow BCs, not just ones needing simulation context — regressed plain impenetrability fills (e.g. \`w=0\`). Fixed by checking each NFBC's own condition via \`normal_flow_needs_simulation_context\`. Full CPU unit test suite passes locally.

## Update 2: distributed GPU \`InvalidIRError\` fix

On distributed GPU, \`fill_halo_regions!(field)\` can be called without \`clock\`/\`model_fields\` during model initialisation (before the clock is live). For \`RNFBC\` fields (\`NormalFlowBoundaryCondition\` with a \`NormalRadiation\` scheme) the call chain reaches \`_fill_*_halo!\` with \`args=()\`. The exact-signature radiation methods don't match, the plain \`NFBC\` catch-all fires, and \`getbc\` tries to call the \`DiscreteBoundaryFunction\` with missing args — causing \`InvalidIRError: call to gpu_gc_pool_alloc\` when the GPU kernel is compiled for the first time.

Fix: add variadic \`_fill_*_halo!(... bc::RNFBC, loc, args...) = nothing\` fallbacks for all six faces. They are more specific than the \`NFBC\` catch-all (\`RNFBC ⊂ NFBC\`) so they intercept the bad dispatch and return \`nothing\`. The exact-signature radiation methods still win at time-stepping when the full \`(loc::FAA, clock, model_fields)\` args are present.

Validated on 4-GPU GH200 simulations (1×4 and 2×2 partitions) — both previously crashed at first kernel compilation with this error.

body:
I used Claude to help prepare this PR. This is the second of the two open-boundary PRs — #5962 added `ObliqueRadiation` for the velocities; this one adds tracer reservoirs. It is independent of #5962 (branches off `main`, touches different files) and can be reviewed in either order.

# Add `TracerReservoir`: open boundary tracer reservoirs

## The problem

A prescribed-value tracer open boundary has no memory. The instant the boundary-normal
flow reverses, water re-entering the domain carries the exterior value `cᵉˣᵗ` — no matter
what just left through that same face. Across a tidal cycle, an eddy brushing the
boundary, or any oscillating flow, that manufactures a spurious tracer flux: the domain
exports its own water and imports someone else's, even when the net displacement over the
cycle is exactly zero.

## What this adds

Inspired by the experience in MOM6, `TracerReservoir` carries one extra value per boundary point, `cʳ`, the concentration of
the water sitting just outside the boundary face. It is relaxed not in time but in
**distance advected**: each step the flow moves `d = |uₙ| Δt` across the face, and `cʳ` is
relaxed over a length scale `L` toward whichever reservoir the flow is filling,

```
cʳ ← (cʳ + a c★) / (1 + a),   a = d / L
```

taken as a backward-Euler step, so it is unconditionally stable for any `Δt`. Target and
length scale follow the flow direction:

- **Outflow** — `c★ = cᴵ` (adjacent interior value), `L = outflow_length_scale`. The
  reservoir fills with the water the domain is exporting.
- **Inflow** — `c★ = cᵉˣᵗ` (prescribed exterior value), `L = inflow_length_scale`. The
  reservoir is flushed toward the external state.

The boundary halo cell is then set to `cʳ`, so returning water carries back what recently
left, converging to `cᵉˣᵗ` only after a length `inflow_length_scale` of sustained inflow.

Each length scale has three regimes, matching MOM6:

| `L` | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `0` (default) | **instant** — `cʳ = c★` every step. Outflow becomes zero-gradient; inflow snaps to `cᵉˣᵗ`. This is the memoryless behaviour of a plain `ValueBoundaryCondition`. |
| `0 < L < Inf` | **finite** — relaxation over the distance `L`. |
| `Inf` | **frozen** — `cʳ` never changes in that flow direction. |

Both length scales default to `0` so `TracerReservoir()` reproduces
the memoryless behaviour exactly and the reservoir is strictly opt-in. There is no
universal value to default to: the useful `inflow_length_scale` is a property of the flow
at the boundary, not of the scheme.

Used like the other `Value` schemes — as the `scheme` of a `ValueBoundaryCondition` on a
`Center`-located tracer field. It carries no condition on the velocities, so it is used
alongside a scheme for the boundary-normal velocity (`NormalRadiation`, `ObliqueRadiation`
or `PerturbationAdvection`) and the barotropic pair.

## The defining property

With `inflow_length_scale = outflow_length_scale = 0`, `TracerReservoir()` is bitwise
identical to a memoryless `ValueBoundaryCondition`: the outflow halo equals the interior
value (zero-gradient), the inflow halo equals `cᵉˣᵗ`. Nonzero length scales interpolate
between that limit and a frozen reservoir, with memory. That equivalence at `L = 0` is the
first test.

## Demonstration

`validation/open_boundaries/tracer_reservoir.jl` runs a uniform, spatially-constant
oscillating flow with zero net displacement per period, so a uniform tracer should be
unchanged by the boundary. The memoryless default loses ~7-8% of the tracer per period —
a real physical loss, not noise, from substituting the exterior value for the water that
just left. A frozen or finite-length-scale reservoir recovers it:

![TracerReservoir vs memoryless](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/enri66/OpenBoundaryTestCases/main/media/tracer_reservoir.png)

## Choosing `inflow_length_scale`

The benefit is **not monotone** — freezing the reservoir is not the best choice and can be
much worse than a finite length scale. A reservoir holds *one number* per boundary point.
During outflow it tracks the boundary concentration; at the reversal it holds whatever
value was there at that instant, then feeds that *constant* back in — while the water that
actually returns is the far tail of what left and has a *declining* profile. Relaxing
toward `cᵉˣᵗ` during inflow mimics that decline, and the length scale at which it matches
is set by the parcel excursion `D = 2U/ω` (for an oscillation of amplitude `U`, frequency
`ω`), not by the width of the tracer structure. Scanning a translating-patch problem over
two patch widths × two excursions puts the optimum at

```
inflow_length_scale ≈ 0.3 D
```

with the error there roughly 8× smaller than memoryless. The scaling is with `D` and not
with the structure width — as it must be for a scheme that relaxes over a distance
advected. It degrades when nearly all of the tracer leaves the domain (`D ≳ 4×` the
structure width), where no single-valued reservoir can help and the optimum is
ill-defined. The docstring says all of this.

`outflow_length_scale = 0` is almost always right: the domain should record the water it
exports immediately, which makes the outflow condition zero-gradient — the standard choice.

## Implementation notes

- **No existing scheme is modified.** The whole addition is one new file plus an export and
  an include. `NormalRadiation`, `ObliqueRadiation` and `PerturbationAdvection` are
  untouched.
- **No new infrastructure.** The reservoir slab is one 2-D array over the boundary face
  (per tracer, per boundary), allocated through the existing
  `materialize_radiation_storage` / `regularize_boundary_condition` hooks. It follows
  `NormalRadiation`'s anchor/latest convention so multi-stage steppers re-step from a
  fixed anchor rather than compounding. Initialized to `cᵉˣᵗ` on the first halo fill,
  matching MOM6's `tres = t`.
- **Independent of `NormalRadiation`'s kernels.** The reservoir update is a single small
  `@inline` function — it does not reuse or duplicate the radiation math. The six
  `_fill_*_halo!` methods are the same per-boundary dispatch every scheme in
  `open_boundary_schemes/` already has (they differ only in which velocity component and
  index they read, and the inflow-sign convention).
- The advecting velocity is taken at the boundary **face**, not one cell into the interior:
  it is the flux through that face that carries tracer across the boundary, and it is what
  MOM6's reservoir uses (`uhr` at the segment face).
- `Value` classification, `Center`-located fields, all six boundaries.

## Testing

Two `@testset`s in `test_open_boundary_conditions_hydrostatic.jl` (all 11 tests in that
file pass; the 9 pre-existing ones are unchanged):

1. **Length-scale regimes**, checked directly on the `reservoir_update` kernel where the
   expected values are exact: instant takes the upstream value regardless of history;
   frozen never moves on inflow; finite is the backward-Euler step
   `(cʳ + a cᵉˣᵗ)/(1 + a)`; a stationary flow advects nothing, so a finite-`L` reservoir
   is unchanged.

2. **Recovers exported water**, end-to-end on a `HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModel` with a
   prescribed, spatially uniform, oscillating flow `u = U₀ sin ωt`. Over a whole period
   the net displacement is exactly zero, so a uniform tracer must be unchanged. The frozen
   reservoir returns exactly what it exported (`1.0000` to `atol = 1e-6`); a memoryless
   boundary manufactures a real deficit (loses several percent of the domain's water in a
   single cycle with zero net displacement); a finite length scale sits between the two.
   The same run with the reservoir on the west boundary and the flow reversed gives the
   same result.
title: Add TracerReservoir: open boundary tracer reservoirs
